replication.target_description: On Track conceptual replication, Table 6 Tobit models for word reading, reading comprehension and spelling, full and reduced samples; row correspondence unresolved.

n.sample_role: Candidate overall final student sample only; no target Tobit analytic N established. Students nested within classes and schools.
n.exclusions: Without parental consent; one control school missing October assessment. Reduced Tobit analyses additionally exclude intervention students receiving 50 or fewer sessions.
n.location: Printed p. 94 Sample; pp. 102–104 Tobit models and Table 6
n.quote:
A total of 2,421 students entered first grade in the two municipalities in the inter-
vention year. Parental permission to participate in the effectiveness evaluation was
given for 89.6% of them. Students without parental consent were offered the interven-
tion if they were identified as being at risk, but they were excluded from the effec-
tiveness investigation. The final sample included 2,170 students (51% boys), of whom
1,687 were enrolled in intervention schools. A total of 102 classes across 41 schools3
participated in the study.

reported_success.quote:
Still, we find a significant intervention effect,
meaning that the proportion of at-risk students in schools that implemented the On
Track program was significantly lower than in control schools after the intervention.

notes:
The p. 18 locator matches PDF p. 18 / printed p. 104, Table 6, visually checked from the rendered PDF. The blank description for audit 65 and generic Early Reading Intervention descriptions for audits 66/67 do not specify outcome or full versus reduced conceptual-replication sample. No row-order or numeric matching used.
Printed Table 6 candidates (Tobit intervention estimate; SE; p; Hedges’ g): word reading full 0.90; 0.45; .047; 0.31, reduced 1.03; 0.48; .031; 0.36. Reading comprehension full 1.19; 0.67; .073; 0.41, reduced 0.94; 0.39; .015; 0.58. Spelling full 1.81; 0.45; .000; 0.46, reduced 2.09; 0.46; .000; 0.54. Each p belongs to the same model as its paired estimate and g. The printed .000 values are preserved as candidates, not changed to bounds. No candidate is assigned to an audit row.
Table 6 does not give analytic N. The Sample section gives 2,170 final students, including 1,687 enrolled in intervention schools, 102 classes across 41 schools. These are study-sample counts, not established target Tobit analytic Ns. Exclusions: students without parental consent; all students at one control school failing to report October pre-assessment. Reduced Tobit analyses additionally exclude intervention students with 50 or fewer sessions (23.3% of intervention students), but no reduced analytic count is printed. No N calculated. Table 5 logistic models give observations 2,106 letter writing, 2,105 phoneme isolation, 2,106 spelling, 2,105 word reading, 2,102 reading comprehension; these separate models cannot establish Table 6 analytic Ns.
Reported success records the authors' overall positive intervention verdict, with smaller effects than the original. It does not assert all Tobit outcomes significant: the authors explicitly note full-sample reading comprehension did not reach .05 (p = .073). Original side unassigned placeholder; original primary source not supplied or inspected.
